mainTopic: Learning that פסח comes only from חולין: the debate of רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא, the rule that a היקש cannot be refuted, and the lessons drawn from ״זֹאת הַתּוֹרָה לָעֹלָה...״.
overview: The משנה rules that a קרבן פסח comes only from חולין (ordinary money), not from מעשר שני money. רבי אליעזר learned this from פסח מצרים, and רבי עקיבא objected on two levels: we cannot learn the possible from the impossible, and even if we could, פסח מצרים had no blood or אימורין on a מזבח. The גמרא explains that each sage argued both on his own view and on the other's. רבי אליעזר answers from פסח מדבר on his own view, and from the פסוק ״וְעָבַדְתָּ״ on רבי עקיבא's view. רב ששת learns from this that a היקש cannot be refuted by reasoning. The study hall asks how something learned by היקש can teach by another היקש, and the answer is that all of פסח is one subject. The גמרא then asks for רבי עקיבא's own source, which is the פסוק ״זֹאת הַתּוֹרָה לָעֹלָה וְלַמִּנְחָה...״ that links all the offerings. From עולה it learns that every offering needs a knife, which is known from the עקידה. From מנחה it learns that the offerings are eaten only by male כהנים, and the testing of which offering this teaches continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the later פסח is different from the פסח in מצרים
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא challenges רבי אליעזר's comparison. פסח דורות needs blood and אימורין placed on the מזבח, but פסח מצרים did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you say the same about the פסח of later generations, which needs its blood put on the altar and its fat parts burned on the altar?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא raises a second objection to רבי אליעזר. He says the two kinds of פסח are too different to compare.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר wanted to learn from פסח מצרים that the later פסח must come from חולין. רבי עקיבא points out a real difference. In מצרים there was no מזבח, so no blood or fat went on one, while the later פסח is a full altar offering. A rule from a simpler case does not automatically carry over to a more demanding one.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסח offering brought in all later generations
Putting the blood of the offering on the altar
The fat parts of an offering that are burned on the altar
Up onto the altar

phrases.english: Can you say so about the Pesach of the generations,
which requires placing of blood
and the fat parts burned upon the altar?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי עקיבא's objections to רבי אליעזר's proof from פסח מצרים, which began before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's proof from פסח מצרים that פסח דורות must come from חולין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source case and the target case are different (no altar service versus full altar service), so the comparison breaks down.
steps.whyThisMatters: This difference between the two offerings is the objection the גמרא later tests against the פסח brought in the מדבר.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the פסוק makes the later פסח like the one in מצרים
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר quotes a פסוק showing that every later פסח must be like פסח מצרים, despite the differences.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The verse says, 'You shall perform this service in this month.' This teaches that all the services of this month must be like this one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers רבי עקיבא's objection by bringing a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר does not deny the difference רבי עקיבא pointed out. Instead, he says the תורה itself tied the later פסח to the one in מצרים with the words 'this service.' Since the פסוק links them, the difference in altar service does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You shall perform this service'; the words that link the later פסח to פסח מצרים
Like this one, meaning like פסח מצרים

phrases.english: He said to him: Behold, it says:
phrases.notes: "He" here is רבי אליעזר answering רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: "And you shall perform this service
in this month,"
meaning that all the services
of this month shall be like this one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי עקיבא's objection from step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural link that overrides the difference between the cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the two kinds of פסח differ in their altar service, we cannot learn one from the other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק 'this service' ties every later פסח to פסח מצרים, so the comparison holds.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר's final source is the פסוק 'וְעָבַדְתָּ אֶת הָעֲבֹדָה הַזֹּאת', which makes every later פסח like פסח מצרים.

steps.title: The גמרא asks: if רבי עקיבא held his first objection, why did he drop it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי עקיבא moved to a second objection if he really held that we cannot learn possible from impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for רבי עקיבא: if he holds that we do not learn what is possible from what was impossible, let him stand by that claim!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions רבי עקיבא's own approach. It sets up a two-sided challenge, and this is the first side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא first objected that we cannot learn something possible from something that was impossible. Then he switched to a new objection about the difference between the two offerings. If his first claim was correct, it was enough to reject the proof, so why did he need a new argument?

keyTerms.meaning: We do not learn a case where something was possible from a case where it was impossible
Let him stand by his statement
He holds that view

steps.confusionAlert: Here "impossible" means that in מצרים there was no מעשר at all, so using מעשר money could not have happened then. That is why רבי עקיבא said you cannot learn from it.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva:
if he holds that we do not derive
the possible from the impossible,
let him stand by his statement!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the debate between the two תנאים to the גמרא's own question on רבי עקיבא's method.
steps.kashyaTarget: The way רבי עקיבא shifted from one objection to another
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If his first argument was valid, it already defeated the proof, so his second argument would have been unnecessary.

steps.title: And if he took it back, פסח מדבר disproves his second objection
steps.stepSummary: Second side of the challenge: if רבי עקיבא gave up his first claim and relied only on the difference between the offerings, the פסח brought in the מדבר shows that difference does not matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he took it back, and the only reason he did not learn from פסח מצרים is that objection, then פסח מדבר will prove otherwise!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its two-sided challenge. Either way, רבי עקיבא's position seems hard to defend.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose רבי עקיבא agreed that we can learn possible from impossible, and his only problem was that the altar service is different. The פסח in the מדבר did have blood and אימורין placed on the altar, yet it was bought with חולין, since there was no מעשר in the מדבר. That case breaks his objection and would support רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: He took back his earlier view
A refutation; a difference that breaks a comparison
The פסח offered in the wilderness, in the second year after leaving מצרים
Will prove; a case brought to show that an objection fails

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא has trapped רבי עקיבא between two options. If he kept his first claim, why did he change arguments? If he dropped it, פסח מדבר disproves his second objection.

phrases.english: And if he retracted,
phrases.notes: He means: if רבי עקיבא gave up his first claim about possible and impossible.

phrases.english: and the reason he did not derive from the Pesach of Egypt
is because of that refutation,
phrases.notes: This is the difference about blood and fat on the altar, from step 1.

phrases.english: the Pesach of the wilderness will prove otherwise!
phrases.notes: That פסח had full altar service, yet it came from ordinary money because there was no מעשר in the wilderness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided challenge that began in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's objection about the difference in altar service (step 1)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: פסח מדבר had blood and אימורין on the altar like פסח דורות, yet it came from חולין. So the difference in altar service cannot be what separates the cases.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the גמרא's need to explain רבי עקיבא's real reasoning in what follows.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's second objection was said according to רבי אליעזר's view
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא really holds we cannot learn the possible from the impossible. His second objection only works within רבי אליעזר's view, and רבי אליעזר answered it with ״וְעָבַדְתָּ״.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was speaking according to רבי אליעזר's view. He meant: 'In my opinion, we cannot learn the possible from the impossible. But even according to you, who say we can, there is a difference. פסח מצרים did not need its blood and אימורין put on the מזבח. Can you say the same about פסח דורות, which does need them?' And רבי אליעזר answered him with the פסוק ״וְעָבַדְתָּ״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 3 and step 4. רבי עקיבא never gave up his first claim; his second objection was only an 'even according to you' argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's real reason is that we cannot learn the possible from the impossible. On top of that, he tells רבי אליעזר that even on רבי אליעזר's own view the comparison fails, because the two offerings were brought differently. So both objections stand together, and neither one cancels the other. רבי אליעזר's reply is the פסוק that ties פסח דורות to פסח מצרים.

keyTerms.meaning: according to his words. Arguing inside the other person's view, even though you don't agree with it.
learning a case where something is possible from a case where it was impossible
putting the blood of a קרבן on the מזבח
the parts of a קרבן that are burned on the מזבח
'and you shall serve/keep' (שמות 13:5). This links every later פסח to פסח מצרים.

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'his' (לִדְבָרָיו) means רבי אליעזר's view, not רבי עקיבא's own. רבי עקיבא is speaking as if he accepted רבי אליעזר's rule, just to show it still doesn't work.

phrases.english: He said it according to the words of Rabbi Eliezer:

phrases.aramaic: לְדִידִי אֵין דָּנִין אֶפְשָׁר מִשֶּׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר,
phrases.english: In my view, we do not learn the possible from the impossible;
but according to you, who say
we do learn the possible from the impossible —
what about the Pesach of Egypt?
It is different, since it did not require putting the blood
and the sacrificial parts on the altar.
Will you say the same about the Pesach of later generations,
which requires putting the blood
and the sacrificial parts on the altar?
And Rabbi Eliezer said to him:
"And you shall keep [this service]."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two-sided question of steps 3 and 4 by explaining that the second objection was said only within רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing: the objection was an 'even according to you' argument, not a retreat from his first position.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא dropped his first claim, or he contradicted himself by making a second objection.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא holds both. In his own view the comparison fails, and even in רבי אליעזר's view it fails because of the blood and אימורין difference.

steps.title: Why didn't רבי אליעזר point to פסח מדבר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אליעזר needed the פסוק when he could simply have said that פסח מדבר proves the blood difference doesn't matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let רבי אליעזר say to him: 'פסח מדבר will prove it!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר's choice of answer. A simpler answer seems to be available: the Pesach brought in the מדבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסח מדבר did need blood and אימורין on the מזבח, just like פסח דורות. Yet it still followed the same rule as פסח מצרים. So it shows that רבי עקיבא's difference doesn't matter, and the גמרא asks why רבי אליעזר used a פסוק instead.

keyTerms.meaning: let him say to him. The גמרא suggests a better answer someone could have given.
the פסח offering brought in the מדבר
will prove. Pointing to a case that knocks down a claimed difference.

phrases.english: But Rabbi Eliezer, let him say to him:
The Pesach of the wilderness will prove it!
phrases.notes: That פסח had blood and parts on the altar, yet it was still brought only from regular, non-holy money. So the difference doesn't matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, לֵימָא לֵיהּ: פֶּסַח מִדְבָּר יוֹכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why רבי אליעזר gave the answer of ״וְעָבַדְתָּ״ in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's choice to answer with the פסוק ״וְעָבַדְתָּ״
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: פסח מדבר had blood and אימורין on the מזבח and still matched פסח מצרים. That disproves רבי עקיבא's difference with no need for a פסוק.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר also answered on two levels
steps.stepSummary: On his own view, פסח מדבר answers the objection. But on רבי עקיבא's view, which rejects learning the possible from the impossible, only the פסוק ״וְעָבַדְתָּ״ works.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered him according to רבי עקיבא's view. He meant: 'In my opinion, we can learn the possible from the impossible. And as for your refutation, פסח מדבר proves it is wrong. But according to you, who say we cannot learn the possible from the impossible, the פסוק ״וְעָבַדְתָּ״ shows it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. רבי אליעזר chose the פסוק because it works even on רבי עקיבא's own view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסח מדבר only knocks down the 'blood and אימורין' difference. It does not help if you reject learning the possible from the impossible altogether. רבי עקיבא does reject it, so רבי אליעזר needed a פסוק that directly compares פסח דורות to פסח מצרים. This mirrors step 5: each sage argued both on his own view and on the other's view.

keyTerms.meaning: a refutation. Pointing out a difference that breaks a comparison.
according to me / in my view
according to you / in your view

steps.whatToRemember: Both sages argued on two levels. רבי עקיבא: 'In my view you can't learn the possible from the impossible. Even in yours, the blood and אימורין difference breaks the comparison.' רבי אליעזר: 'In my view, פסח מדבר removes that difference. In your view, the פסוק ״וְעָבַדְתָּ״ makes the comparison anyway.'

phrases.english: He said it to him according to the words of Rabbi Akiva:
In my view, we do learn the possible from the impossible,
and as for this refutation —
phrases.notes: He means רבי עקיבא's point about the blood and parts on the altar.

phrases.english: the Pesach of the wilderness will prove it wrong;
but according to you, who say
we do not learn the possible from the impossible —
"And you shall keep [this service]."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6 by showing the פסוק was needed for רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two-level answer: פסח מדבר works on his own view, and the פסוק works on the other side's view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: פסח מדבר alone should have been enough to answer רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: פסח מדבר only removes the difference in how the offerings were brought. Since רבי עקיבא rejects learning the possible from the impossible, only the פסוק ״וְעָבַדְתָּ״ can make the comparison for him.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Each sage answered both on his own view and on the other's view, so all four statements fit together.

steps.title: Why not refute the comparison even now?
steps.stepSummary: Even after the פסוק ״וְעָבַדְתָּ״, רבי עקיבא could still object that we cannot learn the possible from the impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even now, let him refute it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges: רבי אליעזר's פסוק still links today's פסח to פסח מצרים. So why doesn't רבי עקיבא raise his same objection again?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's main objection was that we cannot learn the possible from the impossible. The פסוק ״וְעָבַדְתָּ״ still compares פסח דורות to פסח מצרים, so that same objection seems to apply. The question is why רבי עקיבא stays quiet.

keyTerms.meaning: let him refute or knock down the argument
and now, after the פסוק was brought

phrases.english: And even now, let him refute it?
phrases.notes: He means: let רבי עקיבא say again that we can't learn the possible from the impossible.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the outcome of steps 5 and 7, where רבי עקיבא accepted the פסוק ״וְעָבַדְתָּ״.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same weakness he pointed out, learning possible from impossible, seems to exist in the פסוק-based comparison too.

steps.title: A היקש cannot be refuted by logic
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת: this shows that a logical objection cannot be raised against a היקש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: This teaches that one cannot refute a היקש.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers that רבי עקיבא's silence teaches a rule: once a פסוק directly links two things, logic cannot undo the link.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's objection, that we cannot learn the possible from the impossible, is an argument from reasoning. A היקש comes from the פסוק itself, so an argument from reasoning cannot break it. That is why רבי עקיבא did not raise his objection again against ״וְעָבַדְתָּ״.

keyTerms.meaning: this teaches us, this shows
we don't raise logical objections against a היקש
a comparison the פסוק makes directly between two things

steps.whatToRemember: A logical point can knock down a logical argument, but it cannot knock down a היקש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This general rule about how a היקש works is used throughout the laws of קדשים.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:

phrases.aramaic: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת, אֵין מְשִׁיבִין עַל הַהֶיקֵּשׁ.
phrases.english: That is to say: one cannot refute a juxtaposition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Establishes a general rule about how a היקש works
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא's objection should work against the פסוק too.
steps.terutzMaskana: A היקש cannot be broken by logic, so the objection doesn't apply.

steps.title: Can something learned by היקש teach by another היקש?
steps.stepSummary: The study hall asked: today's פסח is learned by היקש from פסח מצרים, so how can it then teach other offerings by היקש?
steps.simpleTranslation: And in the study hall they said: Can something learned by היקש turn around and teach by היקש?
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge comes up in the study hall about the משנה's derivation from פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Today's פסח gets its law from פסח מצרים through the היקש of ״וְעָבַדְתָּ״. The other offerings are then learned from פסח. That looks like a second היקש built on top of the first, which is not allowed in קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: the study hall

keyTerms.term: דָּבָר הַלָּמֵד בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ חוֹזֵר וּמְלַמֵּד בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ
keyTerms.meaning: something learned by היקש teaching something else by another היקש

phrases.english: And in the study hall they said:
But can a matter learned by juxtaposition
turn around and teach by juxtaposition?
phrases.notes: Today's פסח was learned from פסח מצרים; now it would be teaching the other offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְתַרְבִּיצָא אֲמוּר: וְכִי דָּבָר הַלָּמֵד בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ חוֹזֵר וּמְלַמֵּד בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new problem with the היקש that step 9 just defended.
steps.kashyaTarget: Learning the other offerings from פסח דורות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: פסח דורות is itself learned by היקש, so it should not teach by another היקש.

steps.title: All of פסח is one subject
steps.stepSummary: The comparison was said about פסח in general, and פסח מצרים and פסח דורות count as one subject.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said in a general way: all of פסח is one thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is no chain of two היקשים, because פסח is treated as one single subject.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The offerings are compared to פסח as a whole, not to a פסח that got its law secondhand. פסח מצרים and פסח דורות are both just "פסח". So this is not a case of something learned by היקש teaching again.

keyTerms.meaning: it was stated in a general way
one single matter

phrases.english: It was stated in a general manner;
the entire Paschal offering is one matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the subject so there is only one link, not two
steps.terutzHavaAmina: פסח דורות and פסח מצרים are two separate things, so this is a chain of היקשים.
steps.terutzMaskana: פסח is one subject, so no second היקש is involved.

steps.title: Where does רבי עקיבא learn that פסח comes from חולין?
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא rejected רבי אליעזר's proofs, so what is his own source that פסח comes only from חולין?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא, from where does he know that פסח comes only from non-sacred property?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי עקיבא and asks for his own source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא argued against רבי אליעזר's proofs, yet he also agrees that פסח must come from חולין. So he needs a source of his own.

keyTerms.meaning: ordinary, non-sacred property
from where does he know it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva:

phrases.aramaic: פֶּסַח דְּאֵינוֹ בָּא אֶלָּא מִן הַחוּלִּין
phrases.english: that the Paschal offering comes only from non-sacred property,
from where does he derive it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, פֶּסַח דְּאֵינוֹ בָּא אֶלָּא מִן הַחוּלִּין מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defending רבי אליעזר to finding רבי עקיבא's own source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי עקיבא's source that פסח must come from חולין

steps.title: The source: the פסוק that lists all the offerings
steps.stepSummary: He learns it from שמואל's teaching in the name of רבי אליעזר on the פסוק ״זֹאת הַתּוֹרָה לָעֹלָה...״.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from what שמואל said in the name of רבי אליעזר: "This is the law of the עולה, the מנחה, the חטאת, the אשם, the מלואים, and the שלמים."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that groups all the offerings together. It is setting up the next lines, which will explain what each offering in the list teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the פסוק lists the offerings together, a feature of one offering can carry over to the others. The גמרא will now go through the list one offering at a time.

keyTerms.meaning: he derives it
the inauguration offerings of the משכן
peace offerings

phrases.english: He derives it from that
which Shmuel said in the name of Rabbi Eliezer:
"This is the law of the burnt offering and of the meal offering,
and of the sin offering and of the guilt offering,
and of the inauguration offering, and of the sacrifice of peace offerings."

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מֵהָא דְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק ״זֹאת הַתּוֹרָה לָעֹלָה...״, which links all the offerings together.

steps.title: From עולה: all offerings need a כלי
steps.stepSummary: Just as an עולה needs a utensil, so too all the offerings need a utensil.
steps.simpleTranslation: "עולה": just as an עולה needs a utensil, so too everything needs a utensil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the list. The first item, עולה, teaches that every offering needs a כלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the first of the lessons drawn from the פסוק. Whatever is true of the עולה here carries over to all the offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: requires a utensil
just as... so too

phrases.english: "Burnt offering":
just as a burnt offering requires a utensil,
so too all require a utensil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts going through the פסוק quoted in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All offerings need a כלי, just like an עולה.

steps.title: Which utensil is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what כלי this lesson is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which utensil the lesson from עולה means. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "A utensil" is too vague, so the גמרא wants to pin down which one the עולה is teaching about.

keyTerms.meaning: what is it?

phrases.english: What is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of "כלי" in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which utensil the עולה lesson refers to

steps.title: It can't be a bowl for blood
steps.stepSummary: If the utensil is a bowl for the blood, we don't need עולה to teach it, since שלמי ציבור already have a פסוק about basins.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is a bowl, then by communal peace offerings it is also written, "And he put it in basins."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests the utensil is a מזרק, a bowl for the blood, and then pushes the suggestion away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק about the peace offerings at הר סיני already mentions basins for the blood. So the עולה would not be needed to teach a bowl. The lesson from עולה must be about something else.

keyTerms.meaning: a bowl used to collect and throw the blood
communal peace offerings
basins

phrases.english: If we say a bowl,

phrases.aramaic: גַּבֵּי זִבְחֵי שַׁלְמֵי צִיבּוּר נָמֵי כְּתִיב
phrases.english: with regard to communal peace offerings it is also written:
"And he put it in basins."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers and rejects a first answer to step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the כלי is a מזרק
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A bowl is already written by שלמי ציבור, so learning it from עולה would add nothing.

steps.title: The utensil is a knife
steps.stepSummary: Since the bowl option was rejected, the גמרא concludes that the כלי is the knife used for שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the utensil is a knife.
steps.whatsHappening: The bowl idea was just rejected, so the גמרא gives its real answer: the כלי that every offering needs, like an עולה, is a knife for שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison to עולה can't be teaching about a bowl, because שלמי ציבור already have their own פסוק for that. So it must teach something new: every offering has to be slaughtered with a real knife, not with something like a sharp stone or reed.

keyTerms.meaning: A knife, the utensil used for שחיטה
A utensil or vessel

phrases.english: Rather, a knife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the bowl option is rejected in step 16, this gives the accepted meaning of כלי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כלי is a knife for שחיטה.

steps.title: How do we know an עולה needs a knife?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that an עולה itself must be slaughtered with a knife.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for the burnt offering itself, from where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just said all offerings learn the knife rule from עולה. Now it asks how we know that עולה itself needs a knife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You can only compare other offerings to עולה if the rule is clearly true for עולה first. So the גמרא wants the original source for the עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: Itself
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: And the burnt offering itself, from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the base case used in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that an עולה must be slaughtered with a knife.

steps.title: The source is the knife אברהם used at the עקידה
steps.stepSummary: אברהם took a knife to slaughter יצחק, and that was an עולה, so an עולה needs a knife.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "And אברהם stretched out his hand and took the knife to slaughter his son." And there it was a burnt offering, as it is written: "And he offered it up as a burnt offering instead of his son."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the story of the עקידה. אברהם used a knife, and the offering there was an עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof has two parts. The first פסוק shows that a knife was used for the שחיטה. The second פסוק shows that this offering was an עולה. Together they teach that an עולה is slaughtered with a knife.

keyTerms.meaning: A knife (the word used in the עקידה story)
The binding of יצחק
Instead of his son

steps.whatToRemember: Every offering needs a knife for שחיטה. We learn this from עולה, and we know it for עולה from the עקידה.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And Avraham stretched out his hand
and took the knife
to slaughter his son."
And there, it was a burnt offering,
as it is written: "And he offered it up as a burnt offering instead of his son."
phrases.notes: בראשית 22:13. This is about the ram that אברהם brought in place of יצחק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: At the עקידה a knife was used for an עולה.

steps.title: From מנחה: all the offerings are eaten only by male כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The next word in the פסוק, מנחה, teaches that all the offerings in the פסוק are eaten only by male כהנים, just like a מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Meal offering": just as a meal offering is eaten only by male priests, so too all of them are eaten only by male priests.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next word in the same פסוק, מנחה, and draws a new lesson from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern is the same as with עולה. Take a rule that is clear for the מנחה and apply it to all the offerings listed in the פסוק. Here the rule is that only male כהנים may eat them.

keyTerms.meaning: A flour offering (meal offering)
Male כהנים
Just as... so too (a comparison pattern)

phrases.english: "Meal offering":
phrases.notes: This is the next word in the same פסוק, ויקרא 7:37: ״זֹאת הַתּוֹרָה לָעֹלָה וְלַמִּנְחָה...״.

phrases.english: just as a meal offering is not eaten
except by males of the priesthood,
so too all of them are not eaten
except by males of the priesthood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues expounding the same פסוק from step 13, now on its next word.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Like a מנחה, all the offerings in the פסוק are eaten only by male כהנים.

steps.title: Which offering is this lesson about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which offering actually needs this lesson.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which offering this lesson is really needed for. This sets up a test of the possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lesson from a פסוק has to teach something we don't already know. So the גמרא will check each offering to see whether its rule is already known from somewhere else.

keyTerms.meaning: What? (asking for the case)

phrases.english: What is it about?
phrases.notes: He is asking which offering really needs this comparison to מנחה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the purpose of the lesson in step 20, like step 15 did for the עולה lesson.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which offering the lesson from מנחה is teaching about.

steps.title: Testing the first option: חטאת and אשם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to suggest that the lesson is about חטאת and אשם, which will be rejected next.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is about the sin offering and the guilt offering...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up the first option, חטאת and אשם. This only sets up the next move: showing why this option doesn't work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works just like step 16. The גמרא raises a possible case so it can show the case doesn't need this lesson. The reason it is rejected comes at the start of the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin offering
A guilt offering
If (introducing an option to test)

phrases.english: If it is the sin offering and the guilt offering,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first possible answer to step 21 in order to test it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the מנחה lesson is about חטאת and אשם (the rejection comes on the next amud).
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not stated on this amud; the reason continues on the next amud.
